item.research_question: How does the precipitation of ordered L12 intermetallics within the fcc phase of a eutectic Al0.7CoCrFeNi high entropy alloy influence its strain-rate dependent mechanical behavior, specifically yield strength, work hardening, and deformation mechanisms under quasi-static versus dynamic loading?
item.material_system: Al0.7CoCrFeNi (15 at.% Al, 21.25 at.% each of Co, Cr, Fe, Ni) forming a lamellar dual-phase microstructure of fcc + B2 (with B2 containing bcc nano-precipitates), further modified by L12 precipitation in the fcc phase.
item.processing_route: Melting of elemental constituents, homogenization at 1150 °C for 1 h, cold rolling to 30% reduction, annealing at 1100 °C for 5 mins (CR-H condition), and low-temperature annealing at 580 °C for 24 h (CR-H-580 condition).
item.test_conditions: Quasi-static tensile loading at a strain rate of 10−3 s−1 and dynamic compressive loading using a split Hopkinson pressure bar (SHPB) at a strain rate of 2 × 103 s−1.
key_findings: The CR-H-580 condition with L12 precipitates exhibited a yield strength of ~1080 MPa and UTS of ~1370 MPa under quasi-static loading, compared to ~770 MPa YS and ~1090 MPa UTS for the CR-H condition.
Under dynamic loading (2 × 103 s−1), flow stresses reached ~1800 MPa for the CR-H-580 condition without failure up to 20% strain.
The introduction of L12 precipitates resulted in a precipitation strengthening of ~310 MPa, which compares reasonably well with the Orowan model prediction of ~360 MPa.
The steady-state work hardening rate increased from ~3000 MPa in the CR-H condition to >4000 MPa in the CR-H-580 condition.
The strain rate sensitivity (SRS) parameter (m) at 1% flow stress was 0.018 for CR-H and 0.017 for CR-H-580, indicating L12 precipitation did not significantly alter SRS.
Post-deformation analysis revealed that the L12 phase disorders under both quasi-static and dynamic deformation, forming anti-phase boundaries.
High density of twins (approx. 20 nm thick) was observed in the fcc phase under dynamic testing, whereas only fine-scale nano-twins were seen under quasi-static testing.
APT analysis showed L12 precipitates have a radius of ~3–5 nm, a volume fraction of ~9.5% within the fcc lamellae, and a composition of ~56.4 at.% Ni and ~35.8 at.% Al.
item.mechanism: The authors attribute the strength increase to the Orowan dislocation bowing and bypass mechanism by coherent L12 precipitates. The high work hardening is explained by the capability of the lamellar structure to store high dislocation densities at interfaces and the formation of anti-phase boundaries upon L12 disordering. The lack of significant change in SRS is rationalized by the presence of precipitate-free channels near the lamellar boundaries which act as sites for high dislocation storage, and the thermally activated nature of the coherent L12 precipitates.
item.limitations: The text notes that detailed first-principles computational studies are needed to establish the exact site-occupancies of elements within the ordered L12 structure due to the unusually high Al content. It also mentions that the B2 lamellae are not continuous but pinched off at the microscopic scale.
item.future_work: The authors state that detailed first-principles, electronic structure based computational studies need to be coupled with experimental observations to establish the site-occupancies of different elements within the ordered L12 structure.
quotes: Low temperature annealing leads to the precipitation of ordered L12 intermetallic precipitates within the fcc resulting in enhanced strength.
The strengthening contribution due to fine scale L12 is modeled using Orowan dislocation bowing and by-pass mechanism.
Interestingly, the coherent nano-scale L12 precipitate caused a significant rise in the yield strength, without affecting the strain rate sensitivity (SRS) significantly.
